description: From July 2008 the Dutch government forbade Iranians from courses related to nuclear technology. The foreign ministry said it was forbidden 'to grant Iranian nationals access to special training or teaching that could contribute to nuclear proliferation activities in Iran'.
Even Dutch citizens of Iranian descent who held no Iranian passport were barred from nine degree programmes. Nationality of origin, not current citizenship, was the operative test.
energy_note: A Dutch citizen, excluded from a Dutch university, for ancestry.
source_name: Library of Congress Global Legal Monitor

aspect: EXAMPLE - the buildings as well as the courses
description: The policy barred Iranians from an experimental reactor at the Nuclear Research and Consultancy Group in Petten, from URENCO, from the Borssele reactor and from a test reactor at Delft University of Technology.
energy_note: Physically excluded from buildings on your own campus.

aspect: The stated justification, and the real history
description: The government said it was implementing UN Security Council Resolution 1737. The Netherlands was especially sensitive because A.Q. Khan, who helped build Pakistan's bomb, gathered information while working at the Dutch URENCO enrichment plant in the 1970s.
energy_note: Paying for a security failure that happened before you were born.

aspect: EXAMPLE - they sued, and they won
description: Iranian students and scientists demonstrated at the University of Amsterdam on 1 September 2008 and sued, arguing the ban breached Article 1 of the Dutch Constitution. Plaintiffs included Behnam Taebi, a PhD student at Delft, nuclear physics professor Nasser Kalantar of Groningen, and Delft chemistry student Kawe Bitaraf.
energy_note: Named people, who fought it in their own names.

description: A court in The Hague found the policy overly broad and in breach of an international civil rights treaty, holding there was 'no objective and reasonable justification' for targeting Iranian students. The 2010 verdict established that Iranian nationals cannot be excluded from facilities or study programmes on the basis of nationality.
energy_note: A court saying plainly that it was discrimination.
notes: The single most useful precedent in the dataset: nationality-based exclusion tested in court and defeated.

aspect: EXAMPLE - and it came back anyway
description: Years later, following new EU sanctions regulations, the Dutch Immigration and Naturalisation Service halted processing of visa and residency applications made by Iranian citizens. The worst affected were PhD students and applicants in disciplines considered 'sensitive' - a term never clarified.
energy_note: Won in court, and the same thing returned under a different name.
